chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every act of kindness is charity, and the best of charity is that given from the back of affluence (ease), and begin with those you support, and the upper hand is better than the lower hand, and Allah does not blame the one who is in subsistence.'

key_terms.عَنْ ظَهْرِ غِنًى: from the back of affluence (giving from ease)

ai.seo_question: What are the key principles of charity and giving in Shia Islam according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, establishes a broad definition of charity (sadaqah) encompassing all good deeds, while prioritizing voluntary giving from surplus wealth over obligatory alms. It highlights the Shia emphasis on familial duty by instructing believers to begin charity with their dependents, reflecting the principle that strengthening kinship ties (silat al-rahim) is a primary form of benevolence. The narration concludes by validating modest giving, assuring divine mercy for those who give according to their capacity rather than demanding excess.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul A’ala, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Every act of kindness is a charity, and the most superior of the charities is a charity from the back of affluence; and begin by favouring the dependants; and the upper (providing) hand is better than the lower (receiving) hand; and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would not Blame you upon the subsistence’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘

Providing all Benevolent Assistance is charity, and the best charity is a charity provided from an affluent condition. You must begin with your dependents. The upper hand is better than the lower hand. Allah does not blame one for moderation.”’
